score_notes.retention: Rules list cut from 17 s (18%) to 7.7 s (10%), with rule 1 moved into the hook. P1 is contradicted at 5.9 s by the note and at 11.2 s by Odette. P2 sets up its cold hook by 3.8 s ('Which unit is this?', rule 4 makes the question itself the tell), and Odette's real text lands at 5.2 s. The clock is continuous: 5:12 to 5:38 in P1 and 5:45 to 6:04 in P2, with no unmarked jump. Rule three now reads 'if your hall light goes out, stay inside until sunrise', and the lights die in reply order. 'After 3 a.m.' and 'always three' are gone, as are 'lol', the 7A stutter and the whisper direction (now speed 1.0 with vox -6). The P2 peak moved after the lifeline (64%). Measured jolt median is 2.7 s (P1) and 2.5 s (P2); the longest gaps are 4.6 and 5.7 s. Remaining risks: the P2 turn at 39% is early, there are 7 numbers/min, and P1 has 39 words in its first 10 s (median 43.5).
score_notes.reference: Primary refs are now SIEGE-CHAT, MOM-NOTE and DORM-RULES, with HEARSE-P2 kept for sequel mechanics. Every alignment row cites a timestamp checked against the annotated corpus file. The miscitations are fixed: SIEGE-CHAT 2:21 censorship is no longer used for the voice swap, the bookend now cites HEARSE-P1 3:16-3:21.9 and SIEGE-CHAT 4:05-4:08, and the 'only then' misread is replaced by MOM-NOTE 2:01-2:04 for the withheld document. Added: a real casualty proof plus peer pressure (dark accounts in sentence case tag June), a typography voice swap the right way round (lowercase Kowal, then calm capitals), a proximity ladder beside the cost ladder, a held P1 peak image with a push-in, and an outside check moved to the hook with the mechanic in 7 words. Not done: Odette's lifeline was not moved into the clock window. D. Rowe's DM plays that role instead.
score_notes.originality: Gate PASS on research/corpus + research/library/transcripts: the longest shared run with any source transcript is 5 words, and the highest source 5-gram share is 0.02% (7666044652910316833 / 7654526047005723937); the PLAYBOOK itself shares a 7-word run. The gate also passes against our own episodes/ and every other backlog/ folder. Against the pilot, the overlap went from a 12-word run and 2.1% 5-grams to a 5-word run and 0.07%. The premise was rebuilt (option b): no Management, no pinned 7 rules, no 'knocks three times / not home', no dissolved company, no 'never ask' rule five, no closet, no back-against-the-door line, no one-person peephole sting. New pieces: the authority asks for unit numbers in the hook, a paper note from the last tenant forbids it, the debunk is 'we don't have a building office', the hidden space is a locked spare room, and the twist is the torn-off end of the note at sunrise. Titles avoid the pilot's words. Residual closeness: the genre conventions (residents' chat, knocks, peephole) and a written-rules note, which the babysitter backlog episode also has (a fridge note with a password rule).
score_notes.producibility: Both storyboards validate on the Spark (zod, Node 22): P1 has 33 scenes and runs 78.8 s; P2 has 34 scenes and runs 82.7 s. check_storyboards.py reports 'ready' for both (every component registered, audio present on the Spark, max hold 2.7 s). The timeline is measured with Kokoro af_heart at 1.3 on the Spark CPU, and every cue sits on a word timestamp. Voice tracks are built on the Spark (studio/public/episodes/horror-new-building-rules/p{1,2}_voice.wav). Spoken numbers are spelled out, and the phonemes for seven-A/B/C/D/E, eight-A and three-B were checked. No kit edits were needed while the kit is locked: door lamps, the note and rule strips, the slip, the spare-room door and the member list are inline SVG on the kit's own hall geometry, and the clock changes are scene splits. Stills render correctly (out/stills/horror-new-building-rules_storyboard.jpg, hnbr_p1b/p1c/p2/p2c.jpg); the note wrap, the lamp positions and the end-card stamp were fixed after the first look. Three thumbnails are rendered (out/thumbs/horror-new-building-rules/). Not done: full MP4 render and loudness mix (the pipeline/audio house mix is not run; storyboard music and SFX tracks stand in).
